title: Ortiz Exceptional Painting Alternative: Trim & Doors
description: Comparing Ortiz Exceptional Painting with Precision Paint Experts for trim, doors, or shutters? See which enamel and prep questions to ask before you hire.
h1: Ortiz Exceptional Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Trim, front doors, and shutters take the most handling and the most sun. Here is how to compare what different painters plan to put on them.

secondary: front door refinishing north central florida
questions: What paint holds up best on doors and trim in Florida?
Should shutters be removed before painting?

sections.h2: Why the details deserve their own comparison
body: Ortiz Exceptional Painting is one of several painting companies North Central Florida homeowners may be considering, and Precision Paint Experts is glad to be part of that comparison. We do not describe other contractors' work. This page is about the smallest surfaces on a house that get the most attention: trim, doors, and shutters.

These pieces are touched daily, bumped by furniture and pets, and hit by direct sun and rain. A wall can forgive a so-so product; a front door usually will not. That is why the coating and prep for these surfaces are worth asking about separately.

On cabinets, doors, and railings, Precision Paint Experts uses a waterborne urethane enamel, which cures to a hard, washable finish. Exterior trim and siding get 100% acrylic. The specific Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore line is named on the estimate, so you know exactly what is going on each surface.
Our article on painting trim and shutters for durability explains why the order of operations and the sheen choice matter as much as the brand.

Sheen is the other half of the choice. Higher-gloss finishes on trim and doors clean more easily and stand up to hands and pet claws, while flatter walls hide surface imperfections. Most homes pair the two, and the contrast is part of what makes trim look crisp. We list the sheen for each surface on the estimate so walls and woodwork are never confused.

sections.h2: Prep questions to ask about trim and doors
body: Pose these to every painter bidding the job, and look for the answers on the written estimate:
bullets: Will joints be re-caulked and nail holes filled before paint?
Is cracked or failing paint on window frames scraped and spot-primed?
Are doors painted in place or removed, and how is hardware protected?
Will shutters be taken down so the wall behind them is covered too?
How many coats go on each piece?

sections.h2: How we approach the finish carpentry
body: Prep days include sanding, nail pops, re-caulking, and spot-priming, plus rot and fascia replacement where the wood has failed. Cracked paint on window frames is more than cosmetic; our piece on cracked paint on window frames explains why. Two full coats are the baseline, with a third for dramatic color changes.
If you only need the details refreshed, our door and shutter painting and trim and molding painting services can be scoped on their own, without a full repaint.

Interior doors, built-ins, and stair railings are part of the same conversation. They see daily contact, and the enamel used on them should match the durability of the exterior pieces. If you are refreshing kitchen cabinets at the same time, our cabinet painting and refinishing service uses the same enamel family, so the finishes look consistent from room to room.

Every job ends with a punch walk. Anything not right at the final walkthrough is fixed before we close out, and labelled touch-up paint stays with you for future nicks. Ask for a free written estimate covering your trim, doors, or shutters.

faqs.q: Can you paint just my front door and shutters?
faqs.a: Yes. Door, shutter, and trim painting can be quoted as a standalone project.

faqs.q: What finish do you use on interior doors?
faqs.a: We use a waterborne urethane enamel on doors, cabinets, and railings. The product line is named on the estimate.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted trim before painting?
faqs.a: Rot and fascia replacement is part of our prep where it is needed, and it is listed on the estimate before work starts.
